title: Dual group matchers: group_matches_pattern vs GroupFilter
description:
main.rs defines a private group_matches_pattern (line 1094) that is a simpler, different implementation from GroupFilter/matches_wildmat. It is used to decide which external pinning service jobs to enqueue (drain task, lines 767-789 and 893-917).

The two matchers differ in behavior:
- matches_wildmat: full DP wildmat (*, ?, any sequence)
- group_matches_pattern: only handles trailing *, treated as starts_with prefix; a ? is matched literally

A user who puts 'comp.lang.?' or 'alt.?est' in pinning.external_services[].groups expecting wildmat semantics will get silent wrong results — the pattern acts as an exact match against the group name with '?' as a literal character.

There is no documentation warning that ExternalPinServiceConfig::groups uses a different matching engine than GroupsConfig::names. A future maintainer editing the groups field in both places will expect identical semantics.

No config validation catches invalid patterns in ExternalPinServiceConfig::groups (validate_group_pattern is only called for groups.names). So '?' or uppercase chars pass silently.

There is no test for group_matches_pattern itself — the function is only reachable from the drain task, which has no unit test coverage.

Fix options: replace group_matches_pattern with matches_wildmat (one-line change, consistent semantics); or document the restricted syntax explicitly and add a config validation check that rejects ? patterns in external service groups.
